record.title: MIIT sets national design for inclusive compute services aimed at Chinese SMEs
record.summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology issued a national action notice for inclusive computing services for small and medium-sized enterprises. The notice sets a 2028 goal to cover at least 10 of 15 SME industry classes and directs work on pooled and edge compute, storage and network access, flexible card-hour, core-hour and Token billing, compute banks and marketplaces, and encouragement for local compute, storage and network vouchers. These are official policy directions and targets; the notice does not establish funding, awards, SME usage, or economic effects.
organizations: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of the People's Republic of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_PUBLIC_ARTIFACT
claims.text: MIIT issued Notice 工信厅通信〔2026〕14号 on 2026-03-27 and published it on 2026-04-02, establishing the public policy notice and its stated action plan.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The notice sets a year-end 2028 goal to cover at least 10 of the 15 SME industry classes and directs work on pooled and edge compute, storage and network capacity, flexible card-hour/core-hour/Token billing, compute banks or marketplaces, and encouragement for local compute/storage/network vouchers.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The notice does not establish appropriations, local voucher awards, recipients, delivered compute hours, SME adoption, additionality, productivity gains or other economic effects.

evidence_gaps.description: National or local appropriations and implemented service rules linked to the notice have not been established in this bounded review.
Awarded vouchers, recipients, delivered compute/storage/network services and realized utilization are unknown.
SME adoption, additionality and productivity effects have not been measured.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented across the stated sectors, a national program combining shared compute access, flexible billing, storage/network support and local vouchers could materially change the practical cost and availability of AI inputs for SMEs. The score reflects potential consequence of the policy design, not evidence that it is funded, delivered or economically effective.
limitations: The source establishes an official policy design and targets, not that the proposed actions are funded or fully implemented.
No award, disbursement, delivered compute, eligible-firm adoption, use-hour or unit-price records were examined in this review.
No causal evidence establishes additionality, productivity, firm growth or broader economic effects.
The notice is national guidance; local measures may differ in eligibility, award rules, funding and execution.
organizations: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of the People's Republic of China

The notice sets a 2028 goal to cover at least 10 of 15 SME industry classes and directs work on pooled and edge compute, storage and network access, flexible card-hour, core-hour and Token billing, compute banks and marketplaces, and encouragement for local compute, storage and network vouchers. technical.claimed_result: MIIT directs a national inclusive-compute service effort and sets a 2028 target to cover at least 10 of 15 SME industry classes; policy measures include pooled and edge compute, storage and network services, flexible card-hour/core-hour/Token billing, compute banks/marketplaces and encouragement for local vouchers.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official publication documents the policy's stated target and service-design directions. No measured implementation or firm outcomes are established.
technical.mechanism: The notice directs local pooling of idle/distributed compute, SME-oriented compute pools and edge facilities, nearby storage, network access improvements, flexible consumption billing, compute exchange models and local voucher encouragement.
technical.regime: National Chinese MIIT policy notice published 2026-04-02, setting a target through the end of 2028 across at least 10 of 15 SME classification sectors.
technical.reproducibility: The source is a public official policy notice. Its implementation and effects cannot be reproduced from this document alone.
technical.strongest_baseline: The notice gives a future coverage target but no baseline for current SME compute access, prices or use.

brief.title: MIIT sets national design for inclusive compute services aimed at Chinese SMEs
brief.why_it_matters: The notice links SME access to compute with shared supply, flexible billing, storage and network services, and possible local vouchers. If implemented, these instruments could reduce access barriers for firms across multiple sectors. Its coverage target and service design are concrete enough to track against local programs, while the source alone does not show delivery or productivity effects.
